 Macro Minute Video 
 Mon, November 9, 2026 | 7:28PM ET
 Video: Macro Minute: More evidence bottom is in: stocks rally on bad news. And also, VIX term structure uninverted
 Tom Lee, CFA
 AC
 Head of Research
 Share
 Or copy link
 Copy 
 Add as a preferred source on Google 
 In this Macro Minute video, Tom Lee discusses the stock market outlook this week following the early November 2026 selloff, focusing on how equity indices, including the Nasdaq 100, have traded around recent political and company-specific headlines. He reviews market reactions to negative news involving Nvidia (NVDA) and its CEO, as well as commentary about Elon Musk’s business dealings in Texas and the moves in Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX. Lee also notes post-earnings action in selected AI-related and higher-beta technology names and places these moves in the broader context of the AI equity complex.
 The video examines changes in the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) term structure, including a recent inversion and subsequent move back to a more typical shape, and compares this behavior with prior episodes and the Nasdaq 100. Lee connects these volatility signals with macro drivers such as oil prices, interest rates, and the calendar of upcoming US data: the New York Fed inflation expectations survey, October 2026 core CPI, existing home sales, and core PPI, along with scheduled Federal Reserve commentary. The full video provides Lee’s interpretation of these developments, supporting charts, and his detailed market framework.
